alt: octagonal LED matrix PCB shown front and back, with microcontroller, USB-C charging and battery connector
title: Battery-Powered Octagonal LED Matrix
description:
A portable, battery-powered LED display designed by Haizom Studios. The custom octagonal PCB carries a dense matrix of more than 200 LEDs on the front, with all the control, charging and power electronics hidden on the back.

A microcontroller with its own crystal drives the matrix, and an ICSP header allows in-circuit programming and firmware updates in production. A USB-C port charges the on-board lithium battery through a dedicated charger IC with a charge indicator, and a slide switch handles power.

An inductor-based switching converter generates a stable supply for the LEDs from the battery as it discharges, keeping brightness consistent. The layout routes every LED around the octagonal outline at an even pitch, so the display reads as one clean, uniform surface when lit.

alt: Custom Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W handheld gaming console PCB featuring a TFT display, stereo audio subsystem, microphones, battery management, joystick controls, haptic feedback, and USB-C power delivery.
title: Handheld Gaming Console Based on Raspberry Pi Zero 2W
info: Portable Raspberry Pi gaming platform with audio, display, battery management, and haptic feedback.
description:
Designed a custom handheld gaming console based on the Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, integrating audio, display, power management, user input, and haptic feedback into a compact battery-powered platform. The project involved complete hardware design from schematic capture through PCB layout, prototype validation, and production-ready manufacturing deliverables.

The system features a complete digital audio subsystem built around the WM8960 audio codec connected to the Raspberry Pi via the I2S interface. Dual MEMS microphones enable audio capture, while stereo Class-D amplifiers drive external speakers to provide high-quality audio playback. Careful consideration was given to audio signal integrity, grounding, and mixed-signal PCB layout to ensure reliable performance.

User interaction is provided through an analog joystick, multiple debounced push buttons, and a haptic feedback motor driven by an H-bridge circuit, creating an engaging handheld gaming experience. A WS2812B RGB LED provides visual system status indication and user feedback.

The graphical interface is displayed on a 3.5-inch TFT screen driven by the ILI9486 display controller over an SPI interface. The display subsystem was integrated alongside the audio, power, and user-input circuitry while maintaining a compact board footprint suitable for a portable device.

A key aspect of the design was the power architecture. The device operates from a rechargeable lithium-ion battery and incorporates a dedicated charging circuit, battery fuel gauging, and intelligent power-path management. A MAX17048 fuel gauge communicates with the Raspberry Pi over I2C, providing accurate battery state-of-charge information for monitoring and user feedback. The power-path circuitry was designed to allow seamless operation from either the battery or a USB-C power source, enabling uninterrupted use while charging. A high-efficiency TPS61088 boost converter generates stable system power rails for the Raspberry Pi and peripheral devices across the full battery operating range.

Beyond hardware design, complete manufacturing documentation was prepared, including fabrication files, assembly documentation, and bill of materials. Prototype boards were fabricated and assembled in-house for hardware bring-up, debugging, validation, and design verification before the final production package was delivered to the client.
deliverables: Battery charging and fuel gauge implementation
Hardware bring-up, debugging, and validation testing

alt: motor control design and power stage
title: Motor Control and Power stage Design
description:
A compact and efficient motor controller designed by Haizom Studios for smooth and reliable operation. Built to handle dynamic loads with precision, it delivers consistent performance while maintaining high efficiency.

Engineered with intelligent control techniques, the system ensures accurate speed regulation and stable response under varying conditions. Every detail is optimized for performance, safety, and long-term reliability.

From power handling to control logic, the design focuses on simplicity and effectiveness. The result is a controller that performs seamlessly across a wide range of applications.

alt: STM32H7 drone flight controller PCB with ELRS receiver
title: STM32H7 Flight Controller with ELRS Receiver
description:
A compact 50 × 50 mm flight controller designed by Haizom Studios around the STM32H743. It packs sensing, radio link and telemetry onto a single 4-layer board, so the airframe needs no add-on modules.

The core is a 480 MHz STM32H7 paired with an ICM-42688 6-axis IMU and a BMP581 barometer, giving the flight stack fast, low-noise attitude and altitude data. A buck-boost regulator keeps the logic rail stable across the full battery discharge curve.

An on-board SX1280 ExpressLRS receiver handles the 2.4 GHz control link, while an ESP32-C3 adds Wi-Fi and Bluetooth for configuration and telemetry. The layout keeps the IMU away from switching noise and the RF paths short, fitting 114 components onto the board. A matching ESP32-S3 handheld transmitter was designed alongside it.

alt: industrial control PCB with AC-DC supply and Teensy 4.1
title: Industrial Thermal Control System
description:
An industrial control and monitoring board designed by Haizom Studios. It runs directly from mains power and brings temperature sensing, networking and field wiring onto one robust 4-layer board.

An encapsulated AC-DC module generates the 12 V rail, followed by dedicated 5 V and 3.3 V stages, with clear isolation spacing between the mains section and the low-voltage logic. Pluggable terminal blocks make field wiring fast and serviceable.

A Teensy 4.1 handles control and logging, with thermocouple inputs for high-temperature measurement, ambient sensing, a CAN bus interface and Ethernet. The design went through three hardware revisions, refining connector placement, power distribution and networking along the way.

alt: industrial PFC power board with AIF06ZPFC module, EMI filter and bulk capacitors
title: Industrial PFC Power Board (AIF06ZPFC Carrier)
description:
An industrial power board designed by Haizom Studios to host the Advanced Energy AIF06ZPFC, a high-efficiency full-brick power factor correction module rated up to 2.4 kW. The board turns the module into a complete, ready-to-install AC front-end that delivers a regulated 400 VDC bus from a universal mains input.

Everything the module needs around it is integrated on one 4-layer PCB: the input EMI filter, NTC inrush limiting, bulk capacitance, and a bleeder network that safely discharges the high-voltage bus at power-down. An offline buck converter and low-noise 3.3 V LDOs generate the auxiliary supply for the control electronics.

The module's PMBus interface is brought out through an isolated I²C link, so a host system can read status, voltages and faults safely across the isolation barrier. Wide copper pours and over 1,800 stitching vias handle the current and spread heat, with creepage and clearance planned for mains and 400 V spacing. A separate test board was built to validate each stage before integration.

alt: compact robotics motor control PCB with Teensy 4.1 headers
title: Robotics Motor Control Board
description:
A compact motion-control board designed by Haizom Studios for a robotic platform. It drives the actuators, reads position sensors and talks to the main computer over USB-C.

A Teensy 4.1 runs the real-time control loop. The board provides a half-duplex Dynamixel bus for smart servos, a dedicated motor driver stage for DC motors, and Hall-effect sensor inputs with status LEDs for position and homing.

A 12 V boost converter supplies the actuators from a lower battery voltage, while a temperature sensor monitors the board under load. The 81 × 47 mm, 4-layer layout separates high-current motor paths from sensitive sensor lines, keeping the control loop clean.

title: High-Temperature LED Driver Board
description:
A multi-channel LED power board designed by Haizom Studios for lighting in a high-temperature environment. Each channel is individually dimmable over I²C.

AL8860 constant-current buck drivers power each LED string efficiently, keeping brightness stable as temperature and forward voltage change. A PCA9685 PWM controller gives the host independent 12-bit dimming of every channel.

An on-board buck converter and 3.3 V LDO generate the logic supply, so the board needs only one power input and an I²C connection. The 63 × 50 mm, 4-layer layout uses solid ground and power planes to spread heat away from the drivers and keep switching loops tight.

alt: power conversion PCB with custom mounting tabs
title: Power Conversion & Monitoring Module
description:
A power conversion and monitoring module designed by Haizom Studios. It converts, monitors and reports power for the system it sits in, all on one compact board.

An LM61495 synchronous buck converter steps the input down efficiently, while a TPS61088 boost converter generates a higher rail from the same source. Both stages were laid out for high current with short, wide switching loops.

An INA260 precision power monitor measures current, voltage and power over I²C, and an AHT20 tracks board temperature and humidity. The 83 × 38 mm, 4-layer board uses a custom outline with integrated mounting tabs, designed to fit its enclosure exactly.

title: ESP32-S3 Camera & Audio Board
description:
A connected vision and voice board designed by Haizom Studios around the ESP32-S3. It captures images and audio, stores them locally and streams over Wi-Fi.

An ESP32-S3-WROOM-2 module provides dual-core processing and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth. A camera connector, microphone and speaker output turn it into a complete capture-and-playback platform, with a microSD slot for local storage.

GPIO and I²C expanders free up pins for sensors and user controls, and an on-board USB-to-UART bridge makes programming simple. The 4-layer layout keeps the camera and audio paths away from the RF section and switching supplies for reliable wireless range.

alt: 4-layer cellular IoT controller PCB with ESP32, LTE modem and relays
title: 4G LTE Cellular IoT Controller
description:
A mains-powered cellular IoT controller designed by Haizom Studios for remote monitoring and switching where Wi-Fi isn't available. It combines an ESP32 with a 4G LTE modem and on-board relays on a single 4-layer board.

An ESP32-WROVER module with 16 MB flash runs the application, and a SIM7600E LTE modem provides the cellular link. Level shifters bridge the logic between the two. An integrated AC-DC module powers the board directly from mains, with a lithium battery and protected charging circuit as backup.

A buck-boost regulator keeps the supply stable across battery and mains operation, and the relay outputs switch external loads. The 111 × 89 mm layout separates the mains, relay and RF sections, with a USB-to-UART bridge for programming.

alt: 4-layer precharge controller PCB with MOSFET drivers and power inductors
title: High-Voltage Precharge Controller
description:
A precharge controller designed by Haizom Studios for 45–60 V DC power systems. It charges the bulk capacitance of the downstream system in a controlled way, preventing the large inrush current that would otherwise damage connectors and contactors.

An LTC7001 high-side MOSFET driver and a UCC27517 gate driver switch the power stage, while precision comparators and a 2.5 V voltage reference monitor the bus and decide when precharge is complete. A buck power module generates the on-board logic supply from the high-voltage input.

The compact 70 × 46 mm, 4-layer layout uses heavy copper and over 800 vias to carry current and spread heat, with clearances planned for the high-voltage nets.

alt: compact 4-layer battery-powered audio and haptics PCB
title: Compact Battery Audio & Haptics Board
description:
A compact, battery-powered audio and haptics board designed by Haizom Studios for a portable consumer device. It packs audio playback, motor feedback and full battery management into just 65 × 31 mm.

A WM8960 audio codec drives a MAX98306 stereo class-D amplifier, and a DRV8837 motor driver powers a vibration motor for haptic feedback. A MAX17048 fuel gauge reports accurate battery charge to the host.

A lithium charger, TPS61088 boost converter and load switch manage power from the battery. The 4-layer layout fits 114 components into the small outline while keeping the audio path clear of switching noise.

alt: narrow 4-layer ESP32-S3 handheld device PCB with display connector
title: ESP32-S3 Handheld Display Device
description:
A battery-powered handheld device designed by Haizom Studios around the ESP32-S3. The narrow 52 × 126 mm board fits inside a slim handheld enclosure and drives a colour TFT display.

An ESP32-S3 module with 16 MB flash and an external antenna connector provides processing and wireless connectivity. A display header connects an ILI9341 TFT screen, and an I/O expander adds extra buttons and controls.

An IP5306 power-management chip charges the lithium battery and boosts it to a stable 5 V rail, with a USB-to-UART bridge for programming. The 4-layer layout keeps the long, narrow board rigid and the RF section clean.

title: Compact LTE Cellular Board
description:
A compact LTE cellular board designed by Haizom Studios to add mobile connectivity to an embedded product. The 47 × 45 mm, 4-layer board is built around a SIMCom SIM7500A LTE module.

A nano-SIM holder, load switches and several dedicated low-noise regulators give the modem the clean, high-current supply it needs during transmit bursts. MOSFET switching allows the host to power-cycle the modem for reliable long-term operation.

The dense 4-layer layout keeps the RF path short and the power distribution solid, fitting 75 components into a small footprint that drops straight into the host product.

title: LoRaWAN Environmental Sensor
description:
A low-power, long-range environmental sensor designed by Haizom Studios. It measures local conditions and reports them over LoRaWAN, reaching gateways kilometres away on very little power.

A RAK3172 LoRaWAN module handles both the application and the radio link. A BME280 sensor measures temperature, humidity and pressure, and a zero-drift OPA333 op-amp conditions an external analog sensor input.

A low-quiescent-current LDO and an efficient power path stretch battery life, and a Tag-Connect header allows programming without a bulky connector. The 95 × 45 mm, 4-layer board is laid out for low noise and long battery life.
